observations: Photo 0, 1, 2: a white games console with a perforated top and a large circular vent pattern on the right half, the design of the Xbox One S.
Photo 1: front of the console shows the Xbox logo on the right, a front slot for discs, a USB port at the left, and a power button area; it is not shown switched on.
Photo 0 and 2: two wireless controllers with Xbox logos: one white older Xbox One style pad, one blue newer style pad with a share button and clear thumbstick covers.
The white controller is grimy around the grips and sticks; light marks on the console top; otherwise no cracks or broken parts visible.
No screen, game disc, FC26 box, power cable, HDMI cable or storage label is shown.
All photos carry a watermark 'KINGSPLEN GAMING GADGETS POSTED ON JIJI'.

read_from: photo 1 Xbox logo on the console front
photo 0 and photo 2 console design: white perforated top with circular vent and front disc slot, which is the Xbox One S

claims.evidence: Photos 0 to 2 show an Xbox One S console with the Xbox logo in photo 1.
Where the console was used before cannot be shown by photos; a UK plug or label is not shown.
Photos 0 and 2 show two Xbox controllers, one white and one blue.
Photos 0 to 2 show no cracks or broken parts on the outside; only grime on the white pad and light marks.

claims.claim: Comes with FC26 package and other games
claims.evidence: No game disc, box or screen showing installed games is shown.
Photo 0 and 2 show a grimy, worn white controller and marks on the console; it is a used console in fair to good condition.
Case screws and seals are not shown, and internals cannot be seen remotely.
No clip or photo of the console powered on with a picture on a screen.
No receipt or warranty document is shown.

risks.risk: Console does not power on, has a failing hard drive, or overheats.
risks.proof: Clip of the console booting to the home screen on a TV, then opening a game.

risks.risk: Disc drive does not read discs.
risks.proof: Clip of a game disc inserted and starting from the drive.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as with a faulty disc drive.

risks.risk: Storage is the smaller size, not the larger one.
risks.proof: Screenshot of the Settings, System, Storage page or the label on the underside.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as the smallest storage version.

risks.risk: FC26 and other games are digital on the seller's account and leave with it, or are not present at all.
risks.proof: Photo of the FC26 disc in its case, or a screen showing the games installed and licensed to the console.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as console and pads only, no games.

risks.risk: Controllers have stick drift or dead buttons.
risks.proof: Clip of each pad moving the cursor and pressing every button on screen.
Photo of all the cables and items included in the sale.

risks.risk: Console banned from online play or still tied to someone's account.
risks.proof: Screenshot of the console signed in to Xbox network and of the account reset done.

proof_requests: Clip of the console powering on and loading a game on a TV, with both controllers used.
Screenshot of the storage page or a photo of the underside label showing capacity and serial.
Photo of the FC26 disc and any other game discs, or a screen showing them installed.
Clip of a disc loading from the drive.
Photo of the power and HDMI cables included.
response.reason: The photos show an Xbox One S console with two Xbox controllers, so it can be priced now at its worst case as not proven working, smallest storage, and no games. A boot clip, a storage screenshot and the FC26 disc would raise it.
